query: How do I reset the admin password on a locked appliance?

passages.text: To reset the admin password on a locked appliance, connect a serial console at 115200 baud, interrupt the boot loader by pressing Ctrl+C within 5 seconds, then type 'password-recovery' at the prompt. The system will generate a one-time recovery token printed on the console; enter it at the login screen to set a new password. This procedure only works from the physical console; remote access is disabled during recovery.
The appliance supports SNMP v2c and v3. Configure community strings under System > SNMP. Trap destinations are limited to four hosts.
Firmware upgrades are signed with an RSA-4096 key. Unsigned firmware is rejected with error code FW-203.

query: What does LDAP SSO error code 5041 mean?

passages.text: LDAP SSO error 5041 indicates that the user's bind DN was resolved successfully but the subsequent group-membership lookup returned zero groups. This typically means the user exists in the directory but is not a member of any group mapped to an appliance role. Verify the group-to-role mapping in Authentication > LDAP > Role Mapping and confirm the user's primary group is listed.
Error 5040 indicates a bind failure due to invalid credentials. Check the service account password.
Error 5042 is returned when the LDAP server's TLS certificate is not trusted by the appliance's CA store.

query: How can I export system logs for support?

passages.text: System logs can be exported via the web UI under Diagnostics > Log Bundle, or via CLI with the command 'system log-bundle create --output /tmp/bundle.tgz'. The bundle contains kernel logs, application logs, configuration snapshots, and the last 24 hours of telemetry. Upload the bundle to the support portal using the case number as the filename prefix.
The CLI is accessed over SSH on port 22. Only keyboard-interactive and publickey auth are supported.
Telemetry is sent to the vendor over TLS 1.3 every 15 minutes when the 'phone-home' feature is enabled.

query: Which ports must be open for cluster replication?

passages.text: Cluster replication uses TCP ports 7200 (control plane), 7201 (state sync), and 7202 (bulk data transfer). Ensure these ports are reachable between all cluster members on the private replication VLAN. UDP 7203 is used for heartbeat and must also be open; blocking it causes nodes to be declared dead after 15 seconds.
Management traffic uses HTTPS on port 443 by default. This can be changed under System > Network > Management Interface.
DNS resolution is required for cluster member discovery. Configure at least two resolvers under System > Network > DNS.

query: How do I enable FIPS 140-3 mode?

passages.text: FIPS 140-3 mode is enabled under System > Security > Compliance. Enabling FIPS disables non-approved algorithms (MD5, SHA-1 for signatures, RC4, 3DES) and forces TLS 1.2+ with approved cipher suites only. The appliance reboots automatically after the setting is applied. Downgrading from FIPS mode is not supported without a factory reset.
Common Criteria EAL4+ certification covers firmware versions 8.2 and later.
Self-signed certificates are permitted for the management UI but not for SAML or LDAPS.

query: Why does my backup fail with error BK-77?

passages.text: Backup error BK-77 indicates insufficient free space on the backup target. The appliance requires at least 1.5x the current configuration size free on the target volume. Free space under System > Backup > Targets, or select a different target with more capacity. The error is raised before any data is written, so the existing backup set is not affected.
Backup error BK-78 indicates a network timeout reaching the SMB/CIFS target. Check the credentials and retry.
Backup error BK-80 indicates the encryption passphrase is missing from the secure keystore.

query: How do I configure SAML 2.0 with Azure AD?

passages.text: To configure SAML 2.0 with Azure AD, create a non-gallery enterprise application in Azure AD, set the Identifier (Entity ID) to 'urn:appliance:<hostname>', set the Reply URL to 'https://<hostname>/auth/saml/acs', and download the federation metadata XML. Upload this XML under Authentication > SAML > Identity Provider. Map the 'http://schemas.microsoft.com/ws/2008/06/identity/claims/role' claim to the appliance role attribute.
Okta SAML uses a different claim URI; see the Okta-specific guide.
SAML assertions must be signed; encryption of assertions is optional but recommended.

query: What is the supported browser list for the web UI?

passages.text: The web UI supports the latest two stable releases of Chrome, Firefox, Edge, and Safari. Internet Explorer is not supported and is blocked at the login page with a notice directing users to a supported browser. Mobile browsers are supported for read-only dashboards but not for configuration changes.
The web UI requires JavaScript and cookies to be enabled. Third-party cookies are not required.
WebSocket support is required for real-time dashboards; otherwise the UI falls back to 30-second polling.

query: How do I rotate the TLS certificate without downtime?

passages.text: Rotating the TLS certificate without downtime requires first uploading the new certificate and private key under System > Security > Certificates with a staging alias, then binding the staging alias to the management interface. Active sessions are preserved because the appliance supports SNI-based certificate switching at connection time; only new connections will use the new certificate. Once verified, delete the old certificate.
Self-signed certificates can be regenerated from the CLI with 'system cert regenerate-self-signed'.
Certificate CSRs support SHA-256 and SHA-384 signature algorithms; SHA-1 is rejected.

query: How do I troubleshoot high CPU on the data plane?

passages.text: High CPU on the data plane is most often caused by oversized access control lists with many host-granular rules. Use 'show system cpu top 10' from the CLI to identify the top consumers. If acl-engine is at the top, run 'show acl-engine stats' to see rule-evaluation counts per ACL. Consolidating host rules into subnet rules or using address groups typically reduces CPU by 30-50%.
Control-plane high CPU is usually caused by SNMP poll storms; check your NMS polling frequency.
Management-plane high CPU during log-bundle generation is expected and self-resolves within 2 minutes.

query: What is the default session timeout and can I change it?

passages.text: The default web UI session timeout is 30 minutes of inactivity. It can be changed under System > Security > Session Policy to any value between 5 and 480 minutes. An absolute session lifetime of 12 hours is also enforced regardless of activity; this cannot be extended. CLI sessions have a separate 15-minute timeout that is also configurable.
API tokens do not expire by default; set an expiration under System > API > Tokens.
SSH sessions use the system-wide sshd ClientAliveInterval of 300 seconds.

query: How do I upgrade firmware from version 8.1 to 9.0?

passages.text: Upgrading firmware from 8.1 to 9.0 requires an intermediate hop through 8.3 due to a database schema migration introduced in 8.3. Download both 8.3 and 9.0 firmware from the support portal. Upgrade to 8.3 first, verify all services are healthy for at least 10 minutes, then upgrade to 9.0. Direct 8.1 to 9.0 upgrade is rejected with error FW-411.
Firmware downgrade is not supported once the 9.0 schema migration completes.
HA pairs must be upgraded one node at a time with failover between steps.

query: Can I use hardware tokens for 2FA?

passages.text: Hardware tokens using FIDO2/WebAuthn are supported for 2FA under Authentication > MFA > WebAuthn. YubiKey 5 series, Feitian BioPass, and SoloKey V2 have been tested and certified. TOTP is also supported as an alternative or fallback. Hardware tokens are required for privileged roles if the 'high-assurance' policy is enabled.
SMS-based 2FA is supported but not recommended; NIST 800-63B discourages SMS.
Email-based 2FA is disabled by default due to deliverability concerns.

query: How do I integrate with Splunk HEC?

passages.text: To integrate with Splunk HEC, obtain an HTTP Event Collector token from your Splunk instance. Configure the destination under System > Logging > External Destinations with type 'splunk-hec', URL 'https://<splunk>:8088/services/collector', and paste the token. The appliance batches events every 5 seconds; tune under Advanced if you need lower latency. TLS 1.2+ is required.
Syslog RFC 5424 over TCP and UDP is also supported under the same configuration page.
AWS CloudWatch Logs integration requires an IAM role with 'logs:PutLogEvents' permission.

query: What happens during a split-brain scenario in an HA pair?

passages.text: During a split-brain scenario in an HA pair, both nodes believe they are primary because they cannot reach each other or the witness. The appliance uses a quorum-based fencing algorithm: the node with lower cluster-id voluntarily demotes itself to standby and drops all active sessions. If the witness is reachable, it arbitrates and the losing node reboots. Configure a witness under System > HA > Witness.
Standard HA failover takes 3-5 seconds for TCP sessions using connection sync.
Witness-less HA is supported but split-brain recovery requires manual intervention.

query: Is there a REST API for bulk user provisioning?

passages.text: Yes, the REST API supports bulk user provisioning via POST /api/v2/users/bulk with a JSON array of up to 1000 user objects per request. Authentication uses the same API token system as individual endpoints. The endpoint is transactional at the batch level - if any user fails validation, the entire batch is rejected with a per-user error detail in the response. SCIM v2.0 is also supported for identity-provider-driven provisioning.
GraphQL is exposed read-only at /api/graphql for reporting use cases.
Legacy v1 API endpoints are deprecated and will be removed in version 10.0.

query: How do I restrict access to the management interface by IP?

passages.text: Restrict access to the management interface by IP under System > Network > Management ACL. Add allowed source networks in CIDR notation; all other sources will be rejected at the TCP layer before any authentication. Be careful to always include the IP you are currently connected from, and enable the 60-second grace-period safeguard which reverts the ACL if you are locked out and do not confirm the change.
The console port is never subject to the management ACL; it is always available.
Rate limits on failed logins are configured separately under Security > Brute-Force Protection.

query: What database is used for configuration storage?

passages.text: Configuration is stored in an embedded SQLite 3 database at /var/appliance/config.db with WAL mode enabled for durability. The database is replicated synchronously to the HA peer and asynchronously to cluster members. Direct manipulation of the database is not supported and will void the support contract; use the CLI, REST API, or web UI for all configuration changes.
Telemetry and logs use a separate time-series store based on a fork of InfluxDB.
User-session state is kept in memory and is not persisted across reboots.

query: How do I capture a packet trace from the CLI?

passages.text: Capture a packet trace from the CLI with 'diagnostics packet-capture --interface <name> --filter <bpf> --output /tmp/cap.pcap --duration 60'. The BPF filter syntax matches tcpdump. The output file can be downloaded over SCP from /tmp or attached to a support case with 'support attach /tmp/cap.pcap'. Capture is rate-limited to 10,000 packets per second to protect the control plane.
Sustained packet capture for more than 5 minutes is not recommended on production traffic.
Traffic mirroring to a monitoring port is configured under System > Network > Port Mirror.

query: How is data at rest encrypted?

passages.text: Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256-XTS for block storage and AES-256-GCM for object storage. Encryption keys are stored in a hardware TPM 2.0 module with quarterly rotation. Keys can optionally be escrowed to an external KMIP 2.1 key manager such as HashiCorp Vault or Thales CipherTrust. The passphrase for the master key is required only at first boot; subsequent boots unseal automatically via TPM.
Data in transit uses TLS 1.3 with hybrid post-quantum key exchange when enabled.
Log and telemetry data is encrypted with the same scheme as configuration data.

query: What notification channels are supported for alerts?

passages.text: Supported notification channels are SMTP email, Slack incoming webhooks, Microsoft Teams webhooks, PagerDuty Events v2, Opsgenie, generic HTTPS webhook, and SNMP traps. Multiple channels can be configured per alert severity. SMS notifications are supported via a Twilio integration when the 'sms-gateway' feature license is present.
Alert thresholds are configured per metric under Monitoring > Alerts.
Alert suppression windows prevent duplicate alerts during known maintenance periods.

query: How do I validate a configuration backup before restoring it?

passages.text: Validate a configuration backup before restoring with 'system backup validate <file>'. This checks the cryptographic signature, verifies the schema version is compatible with the running firmware, and runs a dry-run apply that reports any conflicts without modifying state. Only backups that pass validation should be restored; restoring an invalid backup can leave the appliance in a partially-applied state that requires factory reset.
Backups older than 90 days may fail validation due to deprecated schema fields.
Cross-model backup restore is not supported; hardware-model metadata is embedded in the backup.

query: Does the appliance support zero-touch provisioning?

passages.text: Yes, the appliance supports zero-touch provisioning via DHCP Option 43 pointing to a TFTP or HTTPS URL that serves a provisioning manifest. On first boot with factory defaults, the appliance retrieves the manifest, applies the base configuration, registers with the cloud management portal, and joins its assigned cluster. The entire process typically completes within 8 minutes from power-on.
ZTP can be disabled under System > Provisioning > ZTP if manual provisioning is preferred.
Cloud-init style user-data is also supported as an alternative ZTP mechanism.

query: How does role-based access control work?

passages.text: Role-based access control assigns users to roles; each role is a named collection of permissions. Built-in roles include Admin, Security-Admin, Network-Admin, Operator, and Auditor. Custom roles can be created with granular permissions on 3,000+ API endpoints. Users can have multiple roles; effective permissions are the union of all role permissions. Permission denials are logged to the audit trail with the specific permission name and requested endpoint.
Service accounts follow the same role model but cannot have interactive login.
The audit trail cannot be modified or deleted even by Admin users; it is append-only.

query: What is the maximum number of concurrent connections supported?

passages.text: The maximum number of concurrent connections depends on the hardware model. The small appliance supports 50,000 concurrent TCP connections, the medium supports 500,000, and the large supports 5,000,000. These are sustained values; peak values may be 20% higher for up to 60 seconds. Connection-table exhaustion triggers an alert at 85% utilization and new connections are rejected above 98% to preserve service for existing sessions.
The session-table size is independently configurable from the connection table.
Connections are removed from the table after 60 seconds of idle for TCP or 30 seconds for UDP.
